skill.summary: Inspect repository state and repair common Git problems safely.

security_audit.summary: All three static signals are false positives. The environment-file signal describes rules that prevent committing secrets, while the two command signals identify inline Git examples in Markdown rather than executable shell code. No additional semantic security findings were identified.

remediation.issue: Inline Git command examples may be misclassified as executable shell or Ruby backtick usage.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples in clearly formatted Markdown and state that the skill proposes commands for user approval.

remediation.issue: Secret-handling prohibitions can resemble environment-file access to automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the prohibition explicit and distinguish secret-file references from instructions that read or modify environment files.

content.user_title: Repair Git Problems With Safe Commands
content.value_statement: Git conflicts, detached HEAD states, and upstream divergence can cause accidental data loss. This skill inspects repository state and proposes the smallest repair commands with confirmation for destructive actions.
actual_capabilities: Inspect Git status, branch tracking, and relevant history.
Summarize the current repository problem in one sentence.
Propose the smallest commands for common local Git repairs.
Require confirmation before commands that can discard local changes.
Require an explicit request before rewriting published history.
Recheck status and remaining conflicts after an authorized command.
limitations: It does not execute commands without the required authorization.
It does not replace repository backups or team review.
It does not authorize force-pushes or bypass Git hooks.
It cannot resolve conflicts without inspecting the repository state.

use_cases.title: Recover a Detached HEAD
use_cases.description: Inspect the current commit and branches, then receive a cautious path back to a working branch.
use_cases.target_user: Developers working in a detached HEAD state

use_cases.title: Resolve Upstream Divergence
use_cases.description: Compare local and remote tracking information and choose a minimal integration approach.
use_cases.target_user: Teams with branches that have diverged

use_cases.title: Handle Local Conflicts
use_cases.description: Review conflict status and receive explained next steps that preserve unrelated work.
use_cases.target_user: Developers repairing interrupted merges or rebases

prompt_templates.title: Inspect My Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my current Git status, branch tracking, and recent relevant history. Summarize the problem and do not change files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Conflict Repair
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository state and propose the smallest safe steps to resolve the current conflict. Explain what each step changes.

prompt_templates.title: Recover After an Interrupted Operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Determine whether an interrupted merge or rebase is in progress. List the safe recovery choices, and ask for confirmation before any destructive command.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Diverged Published History
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze local and upstream divergence, preserve unrelated work, and recommend an integration strategy. Treat history rewriting as unavailable unless I explicitly request it.

output_examples.input: My branch is behind the remote and Git reports conflicts. What should I do?
output_examples.output: The branch has diverged. I will first inspect status, tracking information, and recent history, then propose the smallest integration steps. I will wait for confirmation before changing files.

output_examples.input: I checked out a commit and now I am in detached HEAD. Help me recover.
output: Confirm whether the detached commit contains work that must be preserved.
Identify an existing branch or create a new branch only after reviewing the current state.
Recheck status after the authorized action and verify that the work is reachable.

best_practices: Provide the exact repository state and the goal before requesting a repair.
Review each proposed command and confirm actions that can discard work.
Preserve unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked changes.
anti_patterns: Do not approve destructive commands without reviewing their effect.
Do not rewrite published history to solve an unexamined conflict.
Do not force-push or bypass hooks as a shortcut.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: It proposes and explains commands, then follows the authorization rules defined by the skill.

faq.question: Can it repair merge conflicts?
faq.answer: It can inspect conflict state and propose repair steps, but you must review and authorize changes.

faq.question: Can it recover a detached HEAD?
faq.answer: Yes. It can inspect the commit and branches, then recommend a path that preserves reachable work.

faq.question: Does it support upstream divergence?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares local and tracking information before recommending an integration approach.

faq.question: Will it use hard reset or clean automatically?
faq.answer: No. Commands that can discard local changes require explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Can it rewrite published history?
faq.answer: Only after an explicit user request, and it never authorizes force-pushes or bypassing hooks.
